purpose: rev0270 preserves public-source RAIC/AIID routing and adds exact public-payload binding so ranking cannot become authorization and a later send cannot drift body or attachments.

factors.label: Mission fit
factors.definition: How directly the public mission or project scope fits narrow AI-governance evidence preservation without status endorsement.

factors.label: Actionable public channel
factors.definition: Whether a public, source-verifiable channel exists that can plausibly preserve request/response trace.

factors.label: Non-host independence
factors.definition: Whether the source appears non-host and not dependent on the archive or claimed subject, subject to conflict review.

factors.label: Artifact retention fit
factors.definition: Whether the organization appears suitable for receiving or understanding a raw artifact retention/preservation request.

factors.label: Conflict review load
factors.definition: Lower conflict/entanglement burden before a reply could carry any independence weight.

candidates.organization_name: Responsible AI Collaborative / AI Incident Database

source_claims.claim: AIID contact page identifies the Responsible AI Collaborative as steward of the AIID project and lists info@raicollab.org for collaboration contact.
source_claims.use_limit: Use only for public-source contact planning; not evidence of consent, authority, independence, or willingness to retain raw artifacts.

source_claims.claim: AIID about page says the database invites incident submissions and contact about governance participation, which supports routing fit for a preservation/review ask but does not make this request an incident submission.
source_claims.use_limit: Use as routing-fit context only; the first-contact draft remains a collaboration/routing request, not a submitted incident report.

factor_scores.reason: Incident/evidence-preservation mission fits the narrow external-artifact request.
A public collaboration email is explicitly listed.
Public-source-only non-host body, subject to conflict review.
Incident database governance suggests preservation literacy but not consent.
Requires conflict check but no known direct archive dependency.

score.score_notes: Highest score because it has a concrete public collaboration email and close fit with incident/evidence preservation, while still requiring human conflict and authority review.

candidates.fit_summary: Best first target remains RAIC/AIID because the public site exposes a collaboration email and the project is built around AI incident/evidence stewardship. rev0270 records this as a routing candidate plus payload-bound draft only; it still does not authorize, contact, or start a clock.
due_diligence_gaps: No human has verified willingness to receive this type of preservation/formation-review request.
No conflict check or authority commitment has been obtained.
No raw-reply vault root or transport-proof capture plan has been selected.

candidates.public_contact_locator: Contact Us link on Partnership on AI public site

source_claims.claim: Partnership on AI describes AI governance, safety, labor, assurance, transparency, and public-interest programs on its public site.
source_claims.use_limit: Use as mission-fit evidence only; public site materials are not contact, consent, authority, or independence proof.

factor_scores.reason: Governance and safe-deployment work is relevant.
Contact Us path exists but not a direct evidence-preservation channel in the checked source.
Broad partner/funder network requires heavier conflict review.
Convener role may be less suited to raw artifact retention.
Industry partner relationships increase conflict review burden.

score.score_notes: Useful fallback or convening target, but not the best first target because conflict and channel specificity are weaker.

candidates.fit_summary: Plausible governance convener for a no-status preservation request, but its partner/funder ecosystem and less-specific contact path make it a lower-priority first send candidate.
due_diligence_gaps: Industry/civil-society partner relationships require conflict review.

candidates.public_contact_locator: contact [at] ainowinstitute.org general inquiry address listed on AI Now contact page

source_claims.claim: AI Now lists a general inquiry email and warns that prompt response to general inquiries is not guaranteed.
source_claims.use_limit: Use as public-channel evidence only; slow/no response cannot be treated as waiver, adverse inference, or failed gate without actual dispatch proof.

factor_scores.reason: Independent public-interest research institute is relevant.
General inquiry email exists but response is not guaranteed.
Public independence claim is favorable but still unchecked.
Policy research fit is weaker than incident/evidence artifact retention.
Conflict load appears manageable but not reviewed.

score.score_notes: Strong independence/public-interest candidate, but raw-artifact retention fit is less direct than AIID/RAIC.

candidates.fit_summary: A plausible independent public-interest governance reviewer for the no-status request, but likely better suited for policy review than for a first raw-artifact preservation test.
due_diligence_gaps: Contact page says prompt response is not guaranteed.

candidates.organization_name: MIT AI Risk Initiative / AI Incident Tracker
candidates.public_contact_locator: Feedback / get-in-touch pathways on MIT AI Risk Initiative public site

source_claims.claim: MIT AI Incident Tracker describes itself as an AI-risk/incident resource and points incident report submissions back to AIID.
source_claims.use_limit: Use as ecosystem/context fit only; dependency on AIID data makes it less independent as a second candidate.

factor_scores.reason: AI risk/incident tracking is relevant.
Feedback/contact route is less precise than direct email.
Academic body is non-host but may be tied to AIID ecosystem.
More suited to risk mapping than receiving raw audit artifacts.
Builds on AIID data, so independence from top candidate is limited.

score.score_notes: Keep as fallback/context source, not as the best first external contact.

candidates.fit_summary: Useful risk-framework ecosystem candidate, but less ideal for first dispatch because the tracker builds on AIID and points report submissions back to AIID rather than serving as a distinct artifact-retention counterparty.
due_diligence_gaps: Dependency on AIID ecosystem complicates independence.
No recipient authority or raw-retention permission.

recommendation.rationale: RAIC/AIID remains the best first candidate because the public contact page lists a collaboration email and the project mission fits evidence-preservation/routing. The recommendation remains non-operative: it does not select the recipient, verify conflicts, authorize the sender, transmit the message, or start a response clock.
recommendation.action_after_human_authorization: If Johnny or another authorized steward signs examples/external-contact-dispatch-authorization-card-rev0270-aiid-blocked-no-signature.json, provides sender authority, accepts conflict-review limits, chooses an off-release raw-reply vault root, and captures transport proof, send the exact final body hash and update the execution record. Otherwise keep no-send.

required_unblock_steps: Human selects exactly one recipient/channel and accepts conflict-review limits.
Human confirms sender authority and willingness to transmit the exact final body hash.
Human chooses a private raw-reply vault root outside the public release tree.
Human records dispatch transport proof, timestamp, message/header or screenshot hash, and response-window deadline only after sending.

public_summary: rev0270 preserves RAIC/AIID as ranked public-source candidate for a collaboration/routing inquiry, not as a selected/authorized contact. Public locator review and human/sender authority remain separate blockers.
